items.title: Putin says war 'coming to an end' as Germany rejects his peace mediator

featured_image.name: Putin suggests Russia's war on Ukraine 'coming to an end'

items.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin told reporters on Saturday that he believes the war in Ukraine is "approaching its end," hours after presiding over the most diminished Victory Day parade in Moscow in nearly two decades — one that for the first time since 2007 featured no tanks, missiles, or other heavy military equipment on Red Square. The remarks, made on May 9 amid a U.S.-brokered three-day ceasefire, drew immediate skepticism from analysts who said they were aimed at a domestic audience rather than reflecting any genuine shift toward peace.[1][2]

items.description: A Qatari tanker carrying liquefied natural gas crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, marking the first successful LNG transit through the chokepoint since the US-Iran war began on February 28, according to ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg. items.title: Trump calls Iran's response to US peace plan 'totally unacceptable'

featured_image.name: Trump says war will be ‘over quickly’ as Iran reviews US peace proposal

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Sunday rejected Iran's reply to the latest American ceasefire proposal, calling it "totally unacceptable" and casting fresh doubt on prospects for ending a war now in its fourth month. The dismissal came hours after Tehran transmitted its formal response through Pakistani mediators, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA.[1][2]

The exchange marks the latest failure in a series of proposals and counterproposals traded between Washington and Tehran since a fragile ceasefire took effect on April 8. Despite weeks of shuttle diplomacy involving Pakistan, Qatar and other intermediaries, the two sides remain far apart on core issues including Iran's nuclear program, the fate of the Strait of Hormuz and the scope of American sanctions relief.[3]

items.title: Iran threatens 'decisive' response to UK, French warships near Hormuz

featured_image.name: UK Sends HMS Dragon to the Strait of Hormuz

items.description: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi warned on Sunday that any French or British warships entering the Strait of Hormuz to accompany U.S. forces would face a "decisive and immediate response" from Iran's armed forces, escalating a standoff over one of the world's most strategically vital waterways.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump accuses Iran of 'playing games,' threatens action

featured_image.name: Trump officials whisper that his Truth Social posts about ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Sunday accused Iran of "playing games" with the United States, escalating rhetoric as Washington awaits a formal Iranian response to a peace proposal that could end months of conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump warned that Iran would "be made to stop," following days of tense exchanges in the strait and diplomatic back-and-forth mediated by Pakistan. The president also signaled he may resume "Project Freedom Plus" — an expanded version of the military operation to escort commercial vessels through the waterway — if negotiations collapse.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump set to travel to Beijing for high-stakes Xi summit

featured_image.name: Iran focus at Trump-Xi summit may delay progress on tariffs, rare earths

items.description:
President Donald Trump is set to travel to Beijing on May 14–15 for a two-day summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, marking the first U.S. presidential visit to China in nearly nine years and a meeting that will test the fragile détente between the world's two largest economies.[1][2][3]

The visit, originally scheduled for late March, was postponed as the United States became embroiled in the war involving Iran and the Israeli-allied campaign that has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Trump confirmed last week that the trip would proceed as planned, telling reporters he expects an "amazing" meeting with his Chinese counterpart.[2][4][5]

items.title: Iran sends response to US peace proposal via Pakistan after days of delay

featured_image.name: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with Pakistan's Foreign Minister  Ishaq Dar in Islamabad on Friday as Pakistan continues diplomatic efforts  to facilitate potential US–Iran engagement.

items.description:
Iran has submitted its response to the latest US peace proposal through Pakistani mediators, Iranian state media IRNA reported on Sunday, ending days of anticipation as Washington pressed for a reply that Tehran repeatedly withheld.

The submission comes after President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio both said last week that a response was expected imminently — only for Iran to keep Washington waiting for four consecutive days. As recently as Saturday, there was no indication that Tehran had delivered its answer, with Trump telling a French broadcaster he still expected to hear back "very soon."[1][2]
